title: Dishmachine lease + chemical subscription route for independent foodservice (Auto-Chlor model)
product_service: Low-temp chemical-sanitizing dishmachines and bar glasswashers placed on lease (or customer-owned machines brought onto program), bundled with metered detergent/sanitizer/rinse-aid, scheduled preventive maintenance roughly every 4 weeks, and 24/7 emergency repair.
target_customer: Owner/GM of independent restaurants, bars, daycare centers, churches, small senior-living and school kitchens (1-3 machines each) in Chicagoland.
purchase_motivation: Health-code sanitizing requirement; a broken dishmachine stops service; avoids $5-15k machine capex [E]; one vendor for machine, chemicals and repair.
spending_evidence: Warewashing products were ~13% of Ecolab's $16.1B 2025 consolidated sales (~$2B) [A, WS13-S005]; Auto-Chlor claims 140 branches and >100,000 customers [D, WS13-S006] on a lease + 28-day route-service model [D, WS13-S007].
representative_operators: Ecolab - Global Institutional & Specialty segment $5.96B sales, 22.8% operating margin in 2025 (incumbent economics) [A, WS13-S005]
Auto-Chlor System - ~140 branches, >100k customers, leased machines + chemicals + route service (company claim) [D, WS13-S006]
revenue_mechanism: Monthly bundled fee per account (machine + chemicals + service) or chemical-volume pricing with free dispensing equipment; parts/repairs billed for customer-owned machines.
typical_transaction_value: MISSING verified price; analyst estimate $150-$450 per account per month [E].
direct_costs: Chemicals (distributor-supplied or toll-blended private label), machine depreciation (est. $3-8k per door-type low-temp machine [E]), route technician labor, parts, van.
contribution_profit_note: Est. $90-$220/month per account after chemicals, parts and route labor at ~40-60 accounts per technician [E].
working_capital_note: Machine capex precedes 24-36 months of fee recovery; chemical inventory; restaurant net-15/30 receivables; closures strand placed machines.
sales_cycle: 2-8 weeks; owner-level decision, often triggered by a machine failure or poor service from current vendor.
acquisition_channels: door-to-door to independent restaurants and bars
referrals from restaurant equipment repair techs and used-equipment dealers
customer_accessibility: Buyers are numerous and identifiable from public license data; owner-operators are busy and many are under Ecolab/Auto-Chlor/distributor programs; switching is easiest at a service failure.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: dishmachines available via manufacturer dealers and used market; EPA-registered sanitizers via chemical distributors or toll blenders (private label requires registration work) [E].
competitive_intensity: high - Ecolab, Auto-Chlor, broadline-distributor chemical programs, local chemical dealers.
entry_strategy: Owner-run local responsiveness (same-day service), month-to-month terms, transparent pricing for small independents that national players under-serve; bundle glasswashers for bars.
licenses: No specific Illinois license for dishmachine service identified [E]; sanitizers must be EPA/FIFRA-registered products used per label; new plumbing/electrical hookups may need licensed trades in Chicago [E, unverified]; general liability insurance.
regulatory_barriers: Antimicrobial pesticide labeling/repackaging rules if private-labeling sanitizer; hazmat handling of corrosive concentrates.
operational_risks: Technician hiring; 24/7 emergency coverage; chemical spills/burns; machine reliability.
financial_risks: Restaurant failure rate strands capital; price competition from bundled distributor programs.
geographic_constraints: Route density business; start in one dense suburb cluster or Chicago neighborhood.
founder_expertise: Dishmachine mechanics, sanitation chemistry, food-code requirements, field sales.
staffing: Founder sells and services first ~40 accounts; first technician at ~50-70 accounts; office/dispatch at ~150.
automation_potential: Route optimization, digital service logs for health inspections, dispenser telemetry where available, prospect lists from license data, quoting/billing; hands-on service stays human.
delegation_potential: Good: route technician and sales roles are standard; Auto-Chlor's branch network shows replicable branch model.
scalability: Branch-by-branch replication across Midwest metros; recurring revenue base compounds.
expansion: On-premise laundry chemicals for hotels/nursing homes, housekeeping chemicals, glasswashers, ice-machine subscriptions (WS13-002), beer-line cleaning (WS13-010).
roic_note: ~$40-80k capital (van, tools, first 30-60 placed machines) for $60-250k operating profit implies ~100-300% if account retention holds [E].
critical_assumptions: Independent operators will switch from incumbents for service/price
Private or distributor chemical supply at margins near 40%+
unanswered_questions: Actual monthly pricing charged by Auto-Chlor/Ecolab to small accounts
Used/new low-temp machine cost and service life
Whether Illinois requires any registration for sanitizer distribution
failure_modes: Over-investing in machines placed at failing restaurants
Competing only on price against Ecolab bundles
score_rationale: Resilience 7: sanitation is code-required and chemicals are consumed weekly. Scale 7: a private incumbent runs ~140 branches on the template. Access/entry 5: entrenched national players; wedge is local service. FCF 5: plausible $100-150k by yr 3-5 with 2-3 techs.
preliminary_verdict: advance - recurring consumable route with proven private-company template; validate small-account pricing and chemical supply.

title: Commercial ice-machine subscription (ice-as-a-service) for restaurants, bars, healthcare and hotels
subindustry: Ice machine leasing with included cleaning/repair
product_service: Commercial ice machines (undercounter, modular head+bin, dispensers) placed for a monthly fee that includes installation, sanitizing/descaling 2-4x per year, repairs, replacement and backup ice.
target_customer: Owners/facility managers at restaurants, bars, c-stores, clinics, dental/surgery centers, hotels, senior living, gyms.
purchase_motivation: Ice machines are dirty and failure-prone; health-inspection findings (mold/slime); avoid $3-10k capex [E]; predictable opex.
spending_evidence: Easy Ice publishes subscription prices from $170/mo (undercounter) to $460/mo (large modular) [B, WS13-S008] and has rolled up regional ice-subscription operators across 47 states [D, WS13-S009].
representative_operators: Easy Ice - national ice-machine subscription roll-up, 47 states (company claim) [D, WS13-S009]
Local refrigeration contractors offering lease programs [E]
revenue_mechanism: Monthly subscription per machine (36-60-month typical term assumed [E]); add-on cleaning-only contracts for customer-owned machines.
typical_transaction_value: $170-$460 per machine per month at incumbent list price [B, WS13-S008]; new-entrant realized price likely 10-25% lower [E].
direct_costs: Machine depreciation (purchase price MISSING; est. $3-8k installed [E]), filters, sanitizer/descaler, technician time, refrigeration parts, warranty claims.
contribution_profit_note: Est. $90-$220/machine/month after depreciation and service at list-like pricing [E].
working_capital_note: Each placement requires $3-8k up front recovered over ~2-3 years [E]; equipment financing likely needed for growth; monthly billing in advance possible.
sales_cycle: 1-6 weeks; triggered by machine failure, health citation or new opening.
acquisition_channels: restaurant equipment dealers and repair techs
customer_accessibility: High-urgency moments (failure) create inbound demand; many buyers; national incumbent markets heavily online.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: major ice-machine brands sell through dealers/distributors; dealer agreements may restrict rental programs [E].
competitive_intensity: moderate - Easy Ice nationally, refrigeration contractors locally; many buyers still purchase outright.
entry_strategy: Bundle with dish/chemical route (WS13-001) - same customer, same visit cadence; faster local repair than national subscription firm.
licenses: EPA Section 608 technician certification for refrigerant work (exam-based, federal) [E]; possibly Chicago refrigeration/plumbing licensing for water hookups [E, unverified].
regulatory_barriers: Refrigerant transition rules (AIM Act) affect equipment choice [E].
operational_risks: Repair skill depth; parts lead times; backup-ice logistics in summer peaks.
financial_risks: Capital per account; early cancellations; residual value of used machines.
geographic_constraints: Route density; one metro at a time.
founder_expertise: Commercial refrigeration repair, water treatment basics, equipment finance.
automation_potential: Scheduling, inventory of machine fleet, IoT monitoring on newer machines, billing.
delegation_potential: Technician roles standard but refrigeration techs are scarce and well paid.
scalability: Capital-bound; scale funded by equipment financing and retained earnings.
expansion: Water filtration, beverage equipment, dishmachines, walk-in cooler maintenance.
roic_note: Asset-heavy per account: ~30-60% annual return on machine capital at list-like pricing [E].
critical_assumptions: Machine cost and life allow ~2-3 year payback
Customers accept 3-5 year subscriptions from a new local firm
unanswered_questions: Wholesale machine costs and dealer restrictions
Typical service hours per machine per year
score_rationale: Pricing is published (B) and a roll-up exists, showing durable cash; but capital per account and refrigeration-tech scarcity cap ROIC and delegation.
preliminary_verdict: hold - published pricing (B) and an active roll-up show durable cash, but per-account capex and refrigeration-tech scarcity make it best as an add-on to WS13-001.

title: Point-of-use (bottleless) water cooler and filtered dispenser rental to workplaces

Cintas - workplace water within First Aid & Safety segment [A, WS13-S003]

contribution_profit_note: Est. $35-$80/unit/month after filter and visit costs [E].

competitive_intensity: high - Culligan, Primo/ReadyRefresh, Cintas, local dealers.
entry_strategy: Industrial/warehouse segment where national players bundle less; bundle with first-aid route (WS13-004).
licenses: Plumbing connection may require licensed plumber in some municipalities [E, unverified].

scalability: Moderate; low ticket limits profit per route.
expansion: Coffee service, ice machines, micro-markets, first aid.

failure_modes: Low ticket cannot support sales cost
score_rationale: Good unit economics and delegation, but crowded with national bundlers and small tickets cap FCF.
preliminary_verdict: hold - better as an add-on SKU on a first-aid/hygiene route than a standalone business.

referrals from safety consultants and insurance loss-control reps

founder_expertise: Safety product knowledge, OSHA basics, route sales.

preliminary_verdict: advance - low-capital consumable route with A-level incumbent profitability evidence; core of a multi-SKU workplace route.
